text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.1% today after a sharp three-day decline from its peak of $414.65 on November 13th. The move appears tied to weakening crude oil prices—U.S. oil dropped to $89.62 per barrel today—combined with broader market caution around holiday retail demand. While refineries are running at a healthy 95.2% capacity, the softer oil price reduces the spread between what a refiner pays for crude and what it earns from selling gasoline and diesel, squeezing profitability.

The two-week decline of nearly 7% also reflects conflicting signals: elevated heating oil prices (up 59% year-over-year) might suggest strong demand, but retailers are being cautious on inventory ahead of the holidays, and rising shipping costs are dampening consumer spending. Meanwhile, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—a third U.S. carrier arriving and Iranian escalations—haven't yet pushed oil prices decisively higher, leaving the refiner caught between softer crude and uncertain demand ahead.
